subject: DPA / SCCs review + transfer impact addendum — MedLink Health
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@medlinkhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Donovan <m.donovan@clientlegal.com>, compliance@medlinkhealth.com
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Initial DPA redlines and SCCs packet

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, attached are MedLink's redlines to the DPA and the order form. We've also included our SCCs execution packet and a short summary of the transfer impact items we flagged for this engagement (primarily around KMS key custody, subprocessor routing, and onshore processing carve-outs).

High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood accept the SCCs as executed addenda, or do you need us to adopt the EU Commission Annex approach?
- We're looking for confirmation on processor/processor vs controller/processor mapping in the Order Form (we flagged Section 2.1).
- We need an estimated timeline for evidence (SOC 2 Type II report, subprocessor list, KMS key ownership evidence) — target execution week of Dec 6.

Attachments: MedLink_DPA_redline_v3.docx (redline), MedLink_OrderForm_20271120.pdf (order form), MedLink_SCCs_signature_packet.pdf (SCCs + signature pages).

If you can get a short internal summary back by EOD Monday (Nov 22) that would be ideal — we need to present to procurement on Nov 30.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Legal Operations
MedLink Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@medlinkhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines and SCCs packet

Team — forwarding MedLink's package (see Elena's email below). Quick ask: can Legal + Sales align on a short response that (1) summarizes the redline risk items we can't accept as-is, (2) lists the evidence we can provide immediately, and (3) proposes a narrow transfer impact addendum (TIA) for the remaining items instead of wholesale redlines?

Priority items I see:
- KMS custody / bring-your-own-key ask from MedLink. Do we have a standard KMS statement we can share, or is this a dedicated-capacity only ask?
- SCCs: if we can accept their signed packet it simplifies execution — but procurement will push for Annex approach if counsel requires it.
- Subprocessor list + updated security attestations (SOC2) — must produce.

Ben / Laura — can you take the legal markups and draft a redline counter and a one-page execution checklist we can share with procurement? Priyom, I'll need you to keep MedLink calm on timeline — they want a firm week-of-Dec-6 go/no-go.

Thanks,
Neha
Director, Customer Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Initial DPA redlines and SCCs packet — legal quick take

Neha / team — quick legal take after an initial pass. I pulled out the items that materially change risk or ops and the items we can accept with a short TIA.

Cannot accept as written:
- Their proposed controller obligation in Section 2.1 that would reassign certain liability back to Redwood (we need to keep the processor role consistent).
- Broad KMS requirement that Redwood must hand over key material to the customer — we don't do key escrow for hosted customers.

Can compromise with TIA / narrow addenda:
- KMS: we can confirm cryptographic controls and provide a KMS architecture statement showing customer data encryption at rest and in transit. For dedicated/on-prem customers we can offer BYOK as a supported configuration — need to flag pricing impact.
- Subprocessors: provide current subprocessor list and commit to 30 days' notice of material changes; add a remediation SLA for substantiated incidents.
- SCCs: we can accept their executed SCCs packet if counsel confirms signature pages match. If they prefer Annex approach, we'll require the Annex text be reconciled to our baseline mappings (we should not accept a version that imposes controller-like obligations).

Action items for this thread:
- Laura: produce the legal counter redline (highlight non-starters and TIA language).
- Neha: confirm which evidence we can attach now (SOC2 link, subprocessor list, KMS architecture doc).
- Priyom: ask MedLink to narrow KMS ask to either (a) architecture / certificate or (b) dedicated BYOK option so we can price.

I'll draft the counter and attach a short "execution checklist" that procurement can use to close the loop.

Ben Carter
Sr. Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@medlinkhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood counter + proposed next steps (DPA / TIA)

Hi Elena — thanks for sending these over. We've reviewed internally and attached Redwood's initial counter for the DPA plus a narrow Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) template that addresses the outstanding items for procurement.

What we propose:
1) We accept the SCCs execution packet provided you confirm the signature pages are completed and match the corporate signatory (we attached the matching checklist).
2) We will not agree to KMS key escrow. Instead we can provide a KMS architecture statement and (if you choose dedicated capacity) a BYOK option with additional commercial terms.
3) We'll provide the current SOC 2 Type II report, the full subprocessor list, and a short remediation SLA to be appended as an exhibit.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_counter_v1.docx (redline), TIA_template.docx (narrow addendum).

Can we get your preferences on: (A) SCCs execution vs Annex, and (B) whether you need BYOK or a KMS architecture statement only? If you can confirm by Monday Nov 29 we can get the final counters into DocuSign for signatures the same week.

Thanks — I'll leave the legal details to Ben and Laura, but happy to coordinate procurement timing.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@medlinkhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Donovan <m.donovan@clientlegal.com>, compliance@medlinkhealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood counter + proposed next steps (DPA / TIA)

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the clarity. Procurement counsel reviewed Redwood's counter and prefers to proceed with the SCCs execution packet (faster for our internal approvals). Mark from our external counsel is looping in a single minor point: they want the TIA to explicitly reference the KMS architecture statement as the acceptable evidence for hosted customers (so no BYOK required unless we execute dedicated).

I've uploaded a signed SCCs packet for your records and shared a DocuSign envelope for the Redwood counter (link below). We did accept most of your TIA language with one small edit related to remediation SLAs. Can you confirm Redwood can sign the DocuSign envelope by EOD Wed Dec 1 so we can get procurement approval by Dec 6?

Attachments: MedLink_signed_sccs_packet.pdf
DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.net/MLH-Redwood-Agreement-20271129

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Legal Operations
MedLink Health

Elena — thanks for the update and for uploading the signed SCCs packet. Internal approvals are green on our end pending Ben's final redline revisions to the remediation SLA (he's making a one-paragraph tweak). We'll sign the DocuSign envelope once Ben uploads the final redline (target EOD Wed Dec 1).

What we'll provide now:
- SOC 2 Type II report (link to the report is in our secure drive — I've shared access with your compliance address).
- Current subprocessor list (attached to this email thread for ease).
- KMS architecture statement (attached as a short PDF) — this will satisfy the hosted-hosted confirmation per your counsel.

If procurement needs BYOK for a pilot / dedicated environment, Priyom will follow up with a commercial addendum and pricing. Otherwise we should be able to execute via the SCCs + narrow TIA and have signatures completed by Fri Dec 3.

I'll follow up with the DocuSign confirmation once signed. Thanks all for the quick turnaround.

Neha Kapoor
